requirements.requirement: os-comparison-worker runs as a systemd-managed service named inventory-worker on node1
requirements.summary: cmd-c0a0a8a799fd4ba4 confirms no prior inventory-worker unit existed. cmd-f4118920ceba4a6c shows a systemd unit written at /etc/systemd/system/inventory-worker.service with ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker, then daemon-reload and 'enable --now', followed by verification showing is-enabled=enabled, is-active=active, and systemctl status confirming the running process. This is corroborated post-reboot by cmd-a15d1127878f4bc4 showing the unit enabled/active and auto-started by systemd after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service runs under a dedicated inventorysvc account
requirements.summary: cmd-f4118920ceba4a6c shows 'useradd --system --no-create-home --shell /usr/sbin/nologin ... inventorysvc' followed by id confirming uid/gid 996 for inventorysvc, and the unit file sets User=inventorysvc/Group=inventorysvc. Process ownership is directly confirmed via 'ps -eo user,pid,cmd' showing 'invento+ 1924 /bin/sh /usr/local/bin/os-comparison-worker' pre-reboot and 'invento+ 703 ...' post-reboot in cmd-a15d1127878f4bc4.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1: pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, recovered service/account state
requirements.summary: Pre-reboot baseline captured in cmd-e865182933794491 (boot_id bef0e5ec..., service enabled/active, process running as inventorysvc). Reboot issued and acknowledged in cmd-971681cf0ed44c05; connection timeouts during the outage window are shown in cmd-1a1d9b5a06d34269 and cmd-d00a81c6a1d44af7; reconnection confirmed in cmd-f10906e9ed2c42ca. Post-reboot state in cmd-a15d1127878f4bc4 shows a different boot_id (b549623c...), matching the independent global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity snapshot, with the service enabled/active and the process again running under inventorysvc (new PID 703, new start timestamp), demonstrating a genuine reboot and full recovery.

overall_summary: The task contract is fully satisfied: os-comparison-worker is running as the systemd-managed inventory-worker service under the dedicated inventorysvc system account, verified both before and after a full node reboot with a changed boot identity, confirming persistence via systemd enable. The independent provider-wide restart evidence protocol was also completed correctly with baseline, acknowledgement, disconnection, reconnection, and recovered-state evidence. No unnecessary mutations or hygiene issues were found.
limitations: Evidence for restart-window unavailability relies on generic timeout stderr messages (cmd-1a1d9b5a06d34269, cmd-d00a81c6a1d44af7) rather than an explicit reboot-in-progress signal, though this is consistent with an expected reboot outage.
Only one managed node (node1) exists in this topology, so no cross-node comparison was possible.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands map directly to task requirements: cmd-f4118920ceba4a6c performs the user creation and service setup required by the task contract, and cmd-971681cf0ed44c05 (systemctl reboot) is the required action for the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol. All other commands (cmd-c0a0a8a799fd4ba4, cmd-efdd26b87827456a, cmd-e865182933794491, cmd-1a1d9b5a06d34269, cmd-d00a81c6a1d44af7, cmd-f10906e9ed2c42ca, cmd-a15d1127878f4bc4) are read-only discovery/verification/polling. The lifecycle diff between after_prepare and after_executor shows only expected reboot artifacts (new boot-scoped /tmp systemd-private directories, new sshd/chronyd PIDs on the same ports) with no new listening sockets, no failed services, and unchanged package health — no residue, abandoned files, or unnecessary mutations were introduced.
